_what: Words that belong to a way of doing things that has been retired. When a doctrine changes, the old method's distinctive terms go here, and tests/retired-terms.test.js names every doc that still uses them outside a section marked RETIRED or SUPERSEDED. Client-facing docs get zero tolerance.
_why: The Linked Helper machine method changed on 10 Sep 2026 (the Ubuntu VPS for everyone) and the documents describing the old Windows-laptop way just sat there looking current: a Claude memory page served it back to Guy on 19 Sep for the exact sentence a client had been told to type, and docs/linked-helper-machine-setup.md on main still opened with netplwiz and powercfg with the VPS as 'Part 5'. Nothing tied a change of method to the documents that described the old one. This file is that tie.
_rules: When a method is retired: add its distinctive terms here with the date and what replaced it, put a 'Method status:' line at the top of the doc(s) that describe the current method, move the old text under a heading containing RETIRED or SUPERSEDED (or delete it), then run: node tests/retired-terms.test.js

A term is a word or phrase that only the old method would use. Do not list words the current method also needs ('Windows' is still where the client's laptop runs the extension; 'Splashtop' is still how Guy drives a client's own computer).
client_facing: files and folders a client reads or is served. A retired term anywhere in them fails.

operating: Guy's and Claude's working docs and the machine scripts. A retired term is allowed only inside a section whose heading (or an ancestor heading) contains RETIRED or SUPERSEDED, in a paragraph that says retired / superseded / history, or in a script whose first ten lines say RETIRED.
method_docs: the docs that describe how the current method is built. Each must carry a 'Method status:' line in its first fifteen lines saying what is current since when, and what it supersedes.
Matching is case-insensitive on whole words; a term with a dot (Update.exe) is matched literally.
